When this company depends on a vendor for the ADMT it uses, that vendor's contractual cooperation for access requests is not optional. 11 CCR § 7222(i) requires a service provider or contractor to assist the business in responding to a consumer's ADMT access request. The CPPA's Final Statement of Reasons shows this duty was tightened for clarity, not weakened, during rulemaking. The Agency removed only surplus wording ("key," "generally") from the regulation's own example and cleaned up an internal cross-reference — changes the Agency itself describes as necessary for the regulations' internal consistency, not a narrowing of the underlying duty. Whether this company's vendor agreement actually secures that cooperation is a fact about this company's own contract, not this citation. Section 6 addresses the company's vendor-dependency record. (California Privacy Protection Agency, Final Statement of Reasons, CCPA Updates, Cyber, Risk, ADMT, and Insurance Regulations, 11 CCR § 7222(i), p. 53.)
